nodes.desc: Background launcher. Windows: registers a global hotkey (default Ctrl+Alt+K) + system-tray icon and adds itself to Run for auto-start. macOS: hosts a rumps menu-bar icon. Both spawn kitchensearch.py as a subprocess when the user triggers it. Linux binds a shortcut via the .desktop file instead. Shares picker-settings.json with the app for the hotkey value.

Application entry point. main() loads settings, builds the LicenseManager, constructs the TkPicker, loads the search index once, and runs the front-menu loop dispatching to keyword / semantic / combo / story / favorites / settings. Owns all mode handlers and the copy/copy-at-size/favorite closures passed into the picker (copy-at-size resolves alt→url and calls copy_url_at_size at the requested render size, defaulting to the copy_size setting).

The whole Tk GUI (2800+ lines): borderless half-screen picker, virtualized image result rows with lazy thumbnail loading, dark-mode + zoom, loading/progress bars, story preview, and a small/medium/large copy-size button bar under result views (plus 1-5 digit keys and Ctrl+C) for copying the selected combo at a chosen size. pick_with_images(entries, on_url, on_select, on_favorite, on_copy_size) is the workhorse; on_url is picker_utils.get_thumb, on_select/on_favorite/on_copy_size are closures from kitchensearch.py.
PlaceholderManager: greyed placeholder text for the search Entry, restored on blur. Imported by picker_ui for the filter/search box.
ZoomManager: Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 / Ctrl+MouseWheel zoom factor for the picker UI. Reports the new factor back through on_zoom_change so kitchensearch.py persists it in settings.

apply(root): on Linux registers the bundled Liberation Sans TTF with fontconfig (FcConfigAppFontAddFile) and points every Tk named font at it so UI text renders anti-aliased through Xft. No-op on macOS/Windows which ship good UI fonts.

Shared core hub. load_index() -> entries (url, alt, text); search() keyword ranking; build_base_emoji_index(); get_thumb() download+cache; copy_image_to_clipboard(); copy_url_at_size()/sized_url()/COPY_SIZES for copying a combo at a chosen render size (=sN, native 534 ceiling); record_copy(); favorites read/write; and the split-daemon lifecycle (_spawn_daemon, _daemon_alive, query_daemon over IPC). Calls data_assets.ensure_data() at import.

ensure_data(): on first run, if data/ui_assets/search-index.tsv is missing, unpacks the committed app_assets.tar.gz into ksapp/ (ui_assets/ text corpora + fonts/). Invoked at picker_utils import, by font_setup, and by the split daemon.

LicenseManager: gates Favorites + dark-mode behind a Polar.sh license key. is_licensed() is a fast offline check against cached license.json; activate/validate/deactivate hit Polar's customer-portal API. refresh_async() re-validates in a background thread.
ssl_ctx(): single source of truth for the TLS SSLContext used by every outbound HTTPS call (thumbnail downloads in picker_utils and emoji_story, license API in license.py).

Long-lived semantic-search daemon. load() reads the MiniLM model + all embedding arrays once; then serves newline-JSON requests over a Unix socket / Windows named pipe. 1 word -> squared combo; 2 words -> cross-ranked base combos; then text-embedding cosine fallback. Idle-exits after 600s. Writes a loading-% status file during startup.

MiniLMText: ONNX-runtime wrapper for sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2. load() finds the model in the bundled data/models dir (or the fastembed cache); embed(texts) mean-pools + L2-normalises to 384-d float32 vectors. Used by the split daemon only.

Standalone tool (also spawned as a subprocess by the app). Splits text into phrases, queries the split daemon over IPC for the best combo per phrase, downloads each thumbnail, and composes a phrase-per-row PNG via Pillow written to --output.

Committed tarball shipped with the source. Contains the ui_assets/ text corpora (search-index.tsv, base-emoji-codes/names, embedding-urls/alts, urls.txt) and the fonts/ TTFs. Extracted lazily by data_assets.ensure_data on first run so a fresh checkout has no loose data files.

The keyword-search corpus: one row per emoji-kitchen combo as url \t alt \t text. load_index() parses it into entries for keyword/combo search, and the split daemon parses it into combo_map keyed by the two base-emoji code points. Unpacked from app_assets.tar.gz.

Ordered base-emoji hex code points (codes.txt) with their names (names.txt). The daemon builds code_to_idx from codes.txt so a rank vector over base emojis lines up with base-emoji-minilm.npy. Unpacked from app_assets.tar.gz.

Parallel arrays aligned row-for-row with minilm-pca340.npy: each embedded combo's thumbnail URL (urls.txt) and alt name (alts.txt). The daemon zips them with the cosine scores to return ranked results. Unpacked from app_assets.tar.gz.
Bundled TTFs. Liberation Sans is registered as the anti-aliased Linux UI font by font_setup; Bubblegum Sans is loaded directly by picker_ui for the rainbow title. Unpacked from app_assets.tar.gz.

MiniLM embeddings of each base emoji's name, row-aligned with base-emoji-codes.txt. Dotted with the query embedding to rank base emojis for 1- and 2-word searches. Committed directly (part of the semantic-search data tier, separate from the tarball).
PCA-reduced (340-d) MiniLM text embeddings for every embedded combo, used for the cosine text-similarity fallback ranking. Row-aligned with embedding-urls/alts. Committed directly.
The PCA projection: subtract -mean.npy then multiply by -matrix.npy to map a fresh 384-d query embedding into the same 340-d space as minilm-pca340.npy before scoring. Committed directly.
The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence encoder in ONNX form plus its tokenizer/config, loaded by minilm_text at daemon startup. Committed directly under ksapp/data/models/.

Persisted UI + behaviour settings (menu layout, dark mode, zoom, floating, exit-on-select, default copy size, and the Windows hotkey). Written by kitchensearch.py save_settings and by the daemon's settings dialog; read by both, so it is the single shared config.

User's saved combos as {alt, url, text}, most-recent-first, deduped by url. Written by toggle/add/remove_favorite; read by load_favorites for the Favorites menu. Lives in the config dir (user data), so it survives cache trims.
Cached license state: key, activation_id, valid flag, last_validated_at. LicenseManager.is_licensed() reads it offline; activate/validate/deactivate rewrite it atomically.

Per-URL copy tallies (md5(url) -> {count, alt, variants}) written by record_copy on every clipboard copy. variants lists the md5s of the same combo's other size renders (=sN URLs) so _trim_thumb_cache biases eviction toward keeping frequently-copied images and keeps all size variants of a hot combo warm together.

On-disk cache of downloaded combo thumbnails, named md5(url).png. Each copy size renders a distinct =sN URL, so one combo can have several cached PNGs. Filled by get_thumb (in picker_utils and emoji_story); trimmed to ~200 MB by _trim_thumb_cache, which keeps high copy-count / recently-used images and shares a combo's copy count across all its size variants.

The daemon's runtime coordination files: the Unix socket / named pipe it listens on, the PID record (with start-time for reuse detection) written by _spawn_daemon, and the loading-% status file the picker polls while showing the model-loading bar.
The composed emoji-story image emoji_story writes to --output. kitchensearch.py previews it via picker.show_image and, on Enter, copies it to the clipboard.

Google's Emoji Kitchen image host. get_thumb fetches each combo PNG on demand from the gstatic URL recorded in the search index, then caches it under thumbs/. The only bulk-image source; nothing is pre-bundled.
Polar.sh customer-portal license-key endpoints (activate / validate / deactivate). Public, no API token. LicenseManager posts here to reserve/free an activation slot and to periodically re-validate.

The system clipboard, the app's primary output. copy_image_to_clipboard writes the combo/story PNG via the platform path: CF_DIB+PNG on Windows (ctypes), osascript on macOS, an X11 selection owner (python-xlib) or wl-copy/xclip on Linux.
